summary: Defines a MIB module for managing Ethernet pseudowire services, so tools can model and monitor Ethernet carried across a packet network as if over a wire.

eli5.summary: Ethernet pseudowires make a far-away network connection feel like one cable. This gives a dashboard to check how they are doing.

questions: what is an ethernet pseudowire mib
how to manage ethernet pw with snmp
subtitle: The SNMP MIB module for configuring and monitoring Ethernet carried over pseudowires.

tldr.problem: Operators need a standard way to manage Ethernet pseudowire services, which tie an Ethernet port or VLAN to a point-to-point pseudowire across a packet switched network.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 5603 defines the PW-ENET-STD-MIB module. A per-pseudowire table sets the VLAN mode and VLAN values and links the pseudowire to an Ethernet port, and a statistics table counts illegal VLAN and illegal length packets.
tldr.outcome: It complements the generic PW-STD-MIB and works with any PSN type. It is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

today: RFC 5603 is a Proposed Standard, published in July 2009. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
This document models the management of Ethernet pseudowire (PW) services sent over a Packet Switched Network (PSN). The MIB module is generic and common to all PSN types supported in the PWE3 architecture (RFC 3985), which covers the transport and encapsulation of layer 1 and layer 2 services.

In particular, it associates a port, or specific VLANs on top of a physical Ethernet port or a virtual Ethernet interface (for Virtual Private LAN Service, VPLS), with a point-to-point PW. It is complementary to the PW-STD-MIB (RFC 5601), which manages the generic PW parameters common to all services.

As with other MIB modules, objects are reached through SNMP and defined with SMIv2 (RFC 2578).
sections.eli5: It is a settings panel for a virtual cable that carries Ethernet across a bigger network.

sections.title: Three Layers of MIB Modules
sections.content:
A PW service is managed by three layers of MIB modules working together, following the layering of RFC 3985. The layering isolates PW services from the PSN that carries them, and lets any supported service connect to any supported PSN.

  • The service layer holds service-specific modules that interface with existing MIB modules for the native service. This document defines the Ethernet one.
  • The middle layer is the PW MIB module (RFC 5601), which configures parameters common to all PWs.
  • The PSN layer has a module per PSN type that associates the PW with one or more tunnels. An example is RFC 5602.

The Etherlike-MIB does not support virtual Ethernet ports. To let it manage a PW as an Ethernet port, this module offers an option to give the PW an ifIndex.
sections.eli5: Think of a sandwich. The top slice says what is being carried, the middle says how the virtual cable is set up, and the bottom says which road it travels on.

sections.title: How the Tables Are Used
sections.content:
The module is designed to be agnostic to the PSN type and to support port-based PWs, VLAN-based PWs and VLAN-manipulated PWs. It supports both point-to-point Ethernet services and VPLS. For an MPLS PSN it also supports several PWs carrying one Ethernet service, so that the Ethernet user priority bits can be mapped to the PSN class of service.

The generic pwTable is used for all PW types and a row is typically created by the operator for each PW service. Rows in the PSN-specific module are tied to it by the common pwIndex. If the PW type is Ethernet or EthernetTagged, the agent creates a row in pwEnetTable.

In a typical point-to-point service, pwEnetPortIfIndex links the physical customer-facing port to the PW. Several PWs may be associated with the same physical port. Where it is convenient, the PW can be modeled as a virtual interface of ifType etherLike for statistics and status gathering.
sections.eli5: The operator fills in one row per virtual cable. Another row links it to the real plug on the box.

sections.title: The Objects
sections.content:
The module is rooted at pwEnetStdMIB, { mib-2 180 }. Its pwEnetTable has one row per PW instance with these main objects:

  • pwEnetPwInstance: an index used when several rows map to the same PW. The value 1 SHOULD be used for the first row if the VLAN is not known at creation.
  • pwEnetPwVlan: the service-delimiting VLAN value on the PW. 4095 MUST be used when not applicable, and 0 indicates untagged frames.
  • pwEnetVlanMode: what is done to the VLAN between port and PW, such as noChange, addVlan, changeVlan, removeVlan or portMode.
  • pwEnetPortVlan: the VLAN value on the port side.
  • pwEnetPortIfIndex and pwEnetPwIfIndex: the interface indexes of the port and of the PW as a virtual interface.
  • pwEnetRowStatus and pwEnetStorageType: standard row control.

The pwEnetStatsTable has two read-only counters. pwEnetStatsIllegalVlan counts packets received from the PSN with an illegal, missing or excessive VLAN field, and pwEnetStatsIllegalLength counts packets with an illegal Ethernet length, meaning longer than the advertised MTU or shorter than the allowed size.
sections.eli5: Each virtual cable has a few knobs: which label to use, whether to stick on, swap or peel off a label, and which plug it connects to. Two gauges count packets that look wrong.

sections.title: Service-Delimiting Modes
sections.content:
The RFC lists three main service types for point-to-point use, each shown as a setting of pwEnetPwVlan, pwEnetVlanMode and pwEnetPortVlan.

  • Port mode: all traffic from the port goes to the PW, either as is or with a provider tag added (value 10 in the example).
  • Single VLAN: only the first VLAN field is the service-delimiting tag. Options include keeping it (one-to-one), changing it from 5 to 6, removing it, mapping untagged packets as is or adding a VLAN, and adding a provider VLAN 10 to packets arriving with VLAN 5.
  • Nested VLAN (QinQ): if both the first and second VLAN are service-delimiting, a provider tag 5 can be removed so that traffic with user tag 100 maps to the PW.

Other scenarios are out of scope and are left to other MIB modules that manage the forwarder and Native Service Processing. The bridging between local ports and virtual interfaces for VPLS is also not handled here.

In the worked example in the RFC, a PW for VLAN 5 sets pwEnetPwVlan 5, mode noChange, pwEnetPortVlan 5 and pwEnetPortIfIndex 1001, with the agent setting pwEnetPwInstance to 1.
sections.eli5: The virtual cable can pass sticker labels through untouched, swap one sticker for another, add a sticker or peel one off, depending on how you set it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Objects with read-write or read-create access, such as those in pwEnetTable, provision Ethernet PWs. Unauthorized access could disrupt traffic. Read access may also be sensitive, since the table shows the PW service configuration.

SNMPv3 VACM and USM MUST be used with any v3 agent that implements this module. Deploying SNMP versions before SNMPv3 is NOT RECOMMENDED, and the RFC recommends SNMPv3 with cryptographic security enabled. It is the operator's responsibility to give access only to principals with legitimate rights.
sections.eli5: Anyone who can turn these knobs can break the network, so only trusted people should get the key to the panel.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content: The module uses one IANA-assigned object identifier value recorded in the SMI Numbers registry: pwEnetStdMIB is { mib-2 180 }.
sections.eli5: The module gets its own official number in a master list so it never clashes with others.
